questions.q: What actually backs Auto Loader's record of 'already processed' files at scale?
options: A single text file with one filename per line
A real embedded key-value store (RocksDB) inside the checkpoint, not a flat list
Nothing is tracked — every run rescans the entire directory
A separate SQL database the user must create manually
questions.explain: A flat list of every filename ever seen would itself become slow to scan; Auto Loader uses a real state store to stay fast at scale.

questions.q: What do maxFilesPerTrigger and maxBytesPerTrigger control?
options: The maximum number of columns a schema can have
How much a single micro-batch takes on, useful for controlling backlog catch-up
The total number of streams that can run on a cluster
How often the checkpoint location is backed up
questions.explain: These options cap the size of an individual micro-batch, especially important when a directory has a large existing backlog.

options: Whether a newly started stream processes a directory's existing files or skips straight to only new ones
Whether the checkpoint location is stored in a volume
Whether Auto Loader deletes files after processing them
Whether schema inference runs at all
questions.explain: Setting it to false is the real switch for skipping a directory's historical backlog when starting a brand-new stream.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what did Databricks & Delta Lake Lesson 32 already cover?
options: The RocksDB-backed internal state store mechanism
The core cloudFiles syntax and checkpointLocation, at the level a small example needed
cloudFiles.includeExistingFiles for backfilling
maxFilesPerTrigger and maxBytesPerTrigger throughput controls
questions.explain: This lesson recaps Lesson 32's core syntax before covering the internals and options that example never needed to mention.

questions.q: Why would a naive flat list of processed filenames eventually cause a performance problem?
options: The list itself grows large enough that scanning it becomes slow, defeating the purpose of avoiding a full directory rescan
It has no real downside at any scale
It would cause Auto Loader to delete files by accident
Flat lists are not supported by any file system
questions.explain: At millions of files, checking a flat list for membership becomes its own bottleneck — a real key-value store avoids that.
